slides.1.title: Map of Portuguese Varieties × Regions
slides.1.description: The core geography of the main varieties: Alvarinho (northern Vinho Verde) → Touriga Nacional (Douro/Dão) → Aragonez (Alentejo) → Moscatel (Setúbal)
slides.3.title: Variety × Region Table
slides.3.html:
🍇 Red Varieties × Main Regions

Variety Main regions Character
Touriga Nacional Douro, Porto, Dão Complex floral, high tannin
Touriga Franca Douro Elegant, balanced, red fruit
Tinta Roriz / Aragonez Douro, Dão, Alentejo Red fruit, medium tannin
Baga Bairrada High acidity and tannin, ages well
Trincadeira Alentejo, Ribatejo Deep colour, spice

🍾 White Varieties × Main Regions

Variety Main regions Character
Alvarinho Vinho Verde (Monção) Intensely aromatic, high acidity
Arinto Bucelas, Lisboa, Alentejo High acidity, minerality
Encruzado Dão Complex aromas, ages well
Fernão Pires Tejo, Lisboa Aromatic, easy-drinking
Loureiro Vinho Verde (Lima) Floral, honeyed
slides.4.question: In which Portuguese region is the Baga variety mainly planted?
slides.4.explanation: Baga is the soul variety of Bairrada DOC, known for very high acidity and tannin; with age it can show complex notes of leather, earth and dried flowers.
slides.5.message: Congratulations on completing Lesson 9! You have linked Portugal's varieties to their regions.
slides.5.keyPoints.0: Red varieties: Touriga Nacional (Douro) · Baga (Bairrada) · Trincadeira (Alentejo)
slides.5.keyPoints.1: White varieties: Alvarinho (Vinho Verde) · Encruzado (Dão) · Arinto (Bucelas)
slides.5.keyPoints.2: One variety may have several names: Tinta Roriz = Aragonez = Tempranillo
